status_summary: On 2025-11-13 the White House announced trade framework deals with Argentina, Ecuador, Guatemala and El Salvador, described as strengthening supply chains and trade partnerships in the region, and agreements were signed with El Salvador on 2026-01-29, Guatemala on 2026-01-30 and Argentina on 2026-02-05; the Argentina agreement includes steps against firms owned or controlled by foreign governments and export control cooperation without naming a country. The National Security Strategy released 2025-12-04 (dated November 2025) asks Western Hemisphere partners to help with nearshore manufacturing, seeks stronger hemispheric supply chains to reduce dependence on distant competitors, and names tariffs, reciprocal trade agreements and financing bodies such as the Development Finance Corporation as tools, without a specific relocation program. No program aimed specifically at relocating manufacturing from the PRC was found, and Executive Order 14389 of 2026-02-20 ended the IEEPA duties imposed under nine earlier orders, leaving Section 232 and Section 301 duties in place, after the Supreme Court held that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs.

timeline.event: The White House issued a fact sheet announcing trade framework deals with El Salvador, Argentina, Ecuador and Guatemala to strengthen supply chains and trade partnerships in the region.
The White House released the National Security Strategy (dated November 2025), whose Western Hemisphere section refers to nearshore manufacturing and stronger hemispheric supply chains.
The United States and El Salvador signed an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade; the Guatemala agreement followed on 2026-01-30.

The Office of the US Trade Representative announced the signing of the US-Argentina Agreement on Reciprocal Trade and Investment, which includes economic security provisions on third-country-owned firms and export controls.
Executive Order 14389 ended additional IEEPA tariffs imposed under nine earlier orders; the Supreme Court held the same day in Learning Resources v. Trump that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs.

title: Re-hemisphere manufacturing: shift industry from the PRC to Central and South America
uncertainties: The tariff direction toward Latin America was not mapped country by country (for example Brazil or Mexico), and tariffs applied in 2025 may have cut against the recommendation before the IEEPA ruling. The fact sheet does not mention the PRC, relocation or nearshoring, and the Argentina agreement summary names no country. A tracker lists a Western Hemisphere Nearshoring Act as H.R. 509 in the 119th Congress with no action; congress.gov could not be read, so the bill is a lead only and is not used for the stage. A search for DFC or White House nearshoring initiatives returned only 2020 material and think-tank pieces. The USMCA joint review outcome (left open on 2026-07-01, triggering annual reviews) is reported from a law firm alert. In this review the National Security Strategy (Western Hemisphere section) and EO 14389 (91 FR 9437) were read on whitehouse.gov and federalregister.gov. The 2025 reauthorization of the Development Finance Corporation in P.L. 119-60, reported by CRS and the researcher, is a general finance tool that does not target the Western Hemisphere or manufacturing relocation, and its enrolled text was not read, so it is not counted. The trade agreement signing dates rest on law-firm and accounting-firm pages, not on USTR.
